answer: Identity mills sell packs of keys that share one operator. An applicant stakes 5.80 POA and sits under a public lantern for 22 minutes: every 40 seconds the beacon emits a 7-byte flash, and the applicant echoes a 20-byte HMAC bound to that flash plus a 4-sample uplink plume (delay, jitter, loss, hop hint). After the watch, a 12-minute horizon opens and any three flashes can be re-asked; replies must match the stored plume within 9ms RMSE in 10 seconds. A second key with a near-identical plume, a missed flash, or a late re-ask burns 74% of the stake and blacklists that sketch for five epochs.
